title: The risk technique: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate
blurb: Describe the five steps of the PRINCE2 risk management technique, including the sub-steps inside identify and assess.
question: The project manager is checking whether the combined effect of all risks is within the board's risk tolerance. Which step of the risk technique is this?

teach.body: Formally: the PRINCE2 technique for risk management has five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate. The first four run in sequence and repeat as the project goes on; communicate runs in parallel throughout. In plain English: find the risks, size them up, decide what to do, do it and check it worked, and keep everyone informed all the way through.

teach.caption: Identify, assess, plan and implement are sequential; communicate runs alongside all of them.

items: Define context and objectives: understand which objectives are at risk, and how the business's environment, policies, standards and procedures shape the risk management approach.
Identify the risks: find threats and opportunities and describe each as cause, event and effect.
Prioritize risks: estimate probability, impact on objectives (in their own units), impact on the stage plan, project plan and business case, proximity and velocity.
Assess the combined risk profile: look at aggregated exposure and compare it with risk tolerance and the business's risk appetite.

head: Step
Key work
rows: Context and objectives; threats and opportunities
Action responses; review; correct; owners agreed
Share risk information via existing reports

teach.body: Plan: identify and evaluate the appropriate responses to remove or reduce threats and to maximize opportunities, and decide on monitoring arrangements. Implement: put the planned responses into action, review whether they work and take corrective action where they do not. It is critical in implement that the risk owner and risk action owner are identified and agreed for each risk.

teach.caption: Risk information is shared within the project ecosystem, and with external stakeholders where needed.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a university student records system
teach.body: At Ashgrove University, project manager Lena Fischer first confirms with the board which objectives are at risk: go-live before enrolment and the £1.2m budget (identify). She lists threats such as data migration errors. She rates each risk and checks the total against the board's risk tolerance (assess). The team weighs a trial migration against extra staff (plan). Lena agrees owners and action owners and later checks the trial's results (implement), reporting risks in each highlight report (communicate).

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) 'Define context and objectives' is part of IDENTIFY, not assess. (2) 'Assess the combined risk profile' is part of ASSESS, not plan. (3) Agreeing the risk owner and risk action owner is stressed in IMPLEMENT. (4) Communicate is not a final step; it runs throughout, using existing reports.

items: Five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate.
Identify: define context and objectives, then identify threats and opportunities.
Assess: prioritize risks, then assess the combined risk profile against tolerance and appetite.
Plan: identify and evaluate responses. Implement: action, review, correct; owners agreed.
Communicate runs in parallel, through existing reports.

summary: You can now describe the five steps of the PRINCE2 risk technique and place sub-steps correctly: define context and objectives in identify, the combined risk profile in assess, and agreeing owners in implement. You can also explain that communicate runs throughout using existing reports.

A.q: Which is the correct sequence of the first four steps of the PRINCE2 risk technique?
A.why: The technique runs identify, assess, plan, implement, with communicate running in parallel throughout.

whyNot.0: Risks are assessed before responses are planned.
whyNot.1: Risks must be identified before they can be assessed.
whyNot.3: Planning responses comes after identifying and assessing risks.

A.q: Which step of the risk technique runs in parallel with the others?
A.why: Communicate runs throughout, alongside the four sequential steps.

whyNot.0: Assess is one of the four sequential steps.
whyNot.1: Implement is the last of the four sequential steps.
whyNot.2: Defining context and objectives is the first part of identify, which is a sequential step.

A.q: Which step includes defining the context and objectives?
A.why: Identify starts by defining context and objectives: understanding the objectives at risk and what shapes the risk management approach (9.3.1.1).

whyNot.1: Assess prioritizes risks and assesses the combined risk profile.
whyNot.3: Implement actions responses and agrees owners.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In the [?] step, the combined risk profile is compared with risk tolerance and risk appetite.
B.why: Assessing the combined risk profile is the second part of the assess step.

whyNot.0: Identify defines context and finds risks.
whyNot.1: Plan evaluates responses after risks are assessed.

B.q: In which step is it critical to make sure the risk owner and risk action owner are identified and agreed for each risk?
B.why: The implement step stresses that responsibilities of the risk owner and risk action owner are identified and agreed (9.3.1.4).

whyNot.0: Assess prioritizes risks and looks at the combined profile.
whyNot.2: Identify defines context and describes risks.
whyNot.3: Communicate shares risk information through existing reports.

B.q:
Which two statements about the risk technique are correct?
1. The plan step evaluates responses to reduce threats and maximize opportunities.
2. Communicate is carried out at the end of the project.
3. The assess step includes considering proximity and velocity.
4. Identify includes assessing the combined risk profile.
B.why: Plan evaluates responses (1); assess considers probability, impact, proximity and velocity (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: communicate runs throughout.
whyNot.1: Both are false: communicate is continuous and the combined profile belongs to assess.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the combined risk profile is part of assess.

C.q: A project manager reviews whether a planned response is working and, finding it is not, takes corrective action. Which step is this, and what else is stressed in that step?
options: Implement; agreeing owners for each risk
C.why: Reviewing effectiveness and taking corrective action is implement, which also stresses agreeing the risk owner and risk action owner for each risk.

whyNot.0: Plan evaluates responses before they are actioned.
whyNot.1: Assess prioritizes risks before responses are planned.
whyNot.3: Communicate uses existing reports; reviewing response effectiveness is implement.

C.q: How is risk information communicated, and when?
options: Through a separate risk report, at each stage end
Through existing reports, throughout the project
Through the risk register, at project closure
Through exception reports, when risks are found
C.why: Communicate is continuous and uses existing reports, such as checkpoint, highlight, end stage, end project and lessons reports.

whyNot.0: No separate risk report is needed; existing reports are used, and communication is continuous.
whyNot.2: The register records risks; communication runs throughout, not at closure.
whyNot.3: Exception reports are for forecast tolerance breaches, not every new risk.

C.q: A team checks how the business's own policies and standards will shape the project's risk management approach. Which step is this, and which sub-step?
options: Assess; prioritize the risks by probability
Plan; identify and evaluate the responses
Identify; identify the threats and opportunities
C.why: Understanding the business environment, policies and standards that shape the approach is the 'define context and objectives' part of identify.

whyNot.0: Prioritizing estimates probability, impact, proximity and velocity of risks.
whyNot.1: Evaluating responses comes after risks are assessed.
whyNot.2: Identifying the risks finds threats and opportunities; context comes first.

reteach.title: Organizing a village fun run
reteach.question: What would the five risk steps look like for a fun run?

blocks.body: Identify: agree what success means (500 runners, no injuries, £5k raised) and list what might go wrong or right. Assess: rate each risk and check the overall picture is acceptable. Plan: choose responses, such as first aiders and a rain route. Implement: book them, name who looks after each risk, check it works. Communicate: keep volunteers and the council updated at every meeting.

blocks.text: Agreeing what success means comes first, inside identify.

explain.body: Define context and objectives, then identify threats and opportunities as cause, event and effect.

test.q: What is done in the identify step after defining context and objectives?
options: The combined risk profile is assessed
Risk owners are agreed for each risk
test.why: After defining context and objectives, the identify step finds threats and opportunities.

whyNot.1: That is the second part of assess.

explain.body: Prioritize risks (probability, impact, proximity, velocity), then assess the combined risk profile.

test.q: Which is part of the assess step?
options: Evaluating possible responses to each threat
Reviewing how effective each response has been
Prioritizing risks by probability and impact
Defining the objectives that are at risk
test.why: Assess prioritizes risks by probability, impact, proximity and velocity, then looks at the combined profile.

whyNot.3: Defining objectives at risk is identify.

explain.body: Plan evaluates responses; implement actions them, reviews them and agrees owners.

test.q: What happens in the plan step?
options: Risks are described as cause, event and effect
Appropriate responses are identified and evaluated
Responses are actioned and their effectiveness reviewed
Risk information is shared with external stakeholders
test.why: Plan identifies and evaluates the appropriate responses to remove or reduce threats and maximize opportunities.

explain.body: Continuous, through existing reports, within the project ecosystem and to external stakeholders where needed.

test.q: Which reports are used to communicate risk information?
options: A dedicated risk report produced monthly
The project brief and the project mandate
Existing reports such as highlight reports
test.why: Communicate uses existing reports, such as checkpoint, highlight, end stage, end project and lessons reports.

whyNot.0: No dedicated risk report is required; existing reports carry risk information.
whyNot.1: The approach describes the procedure; it is not the communication channel.
whyNot.2: These are early products, not the ongoing channel for risk information.
